sites.name: Keo Pagoda (Than Quang Tu)
sites.event: An ancient pagoda with the most unique wooden architecture in Vietnam (especially the bell tower), a Special National Relic, and the place of worship for Zen Master Duong Khong Lo.

sites.name: Tran Temple Relic Site (Thai Binh)
sites.event: The birthplace of the Tran Dynasty, housing the tombs of the early Tran kings and Grand Tutor Tran Thu Do.

sites.name: Con Vanh Beach
sites.event: Located within the UNESCO-recognized Red River Delta Biosphere Reserve, famous for its mangrove ecosystem and pristine beach.

sites.name: Con Den Eco-tourism Area
sites.event: Known as the 'Most beautiful coastal dune in the North' with lush green pine forests and the longest bamboo bridge system through a mangrove forest in Vietnam.

sites.name: Tien La Temple
sites.event: The place of worship for General Bat Nan Vu Thi Thuc (a female general under the Hai Ba Trung sisters) who made great contributions to driving out the Eastern Han invaders.

sites.name: Dong Bang Temple (Duc Vua Cha Temple)
sites.event: The place of worship for King Father Bat Hai Dong Dinh, one of the largest centers of the Four Palaces (Dao Mau) belief in the Northern region.

sites.name: Bach Thuan Garden Village
sites.event: A typical ancient garden village of the Northern Delta with a system of ancient houses, ornamental gardens, and sericulture.

sites.name: Dong Chau Beach
sites.event: Famous for its vast clam farming fields stretching as far as the eye can see, creating a unique 'infinity sea' landscape at dawn.

sites.name: Dong Xam Silver Carving Craft Village
sites.event: A famous traditional craft village over 400 years old, home to Dong Xam Temple which worships the craft's founder Nguyen Kim Lau.

sites.name: Le Quy Don Scholar Memorial Area
sites.event: The place of worship and preservation of memorabilia and works of Le Quy Don - a great scholar of Vietnam during the feudal period.

sites.name: Thai Binh Cathedral
sites.event: One of the most beautiful and magnificent cathedrals in Vietnam, inaugurated in 2007, serving as the center of the Thai Binh Diocese.
